messages.content: What are the key factors affecting our profit margin and what actions can we take to improve it?

Based on analysis from Finance, Operations, and Market Intelligence agents, here are the key factors affecting your profit margin:

1. Rising raw material costs (+18% this year)
2. Increased logistics expenses (+12%)
3. Price competition in the electronics segment
4. Higher warranty and return costs

Recommended actions:
• Negotiate long-term supplier contracts
• Optimize logistics routes and warehouse allocation
• Consider 3-5% price adjustment for premium products
• Reduce defect rate through quality control (potential 4-6% margin gain)

agentBreakdowns.finding: Operating expenses grew by 8.4% YoY while top-line average selling price stayed flat, eroding gross margin by 210 bps.
Semiconductor component procurement and coastal port freight surcharges drove 63% of the total expense spike.
Competitors raised prices by 4.2% last month without sacrificing demand elasticity in tier 2 urban centers.
Single-supplier reliance on Silicon Packagers Ltd accounts for 45% of component price volatility.
Dual-sourcing contract renegotiation combined with a 4% premium product price recalibration will restore profit margin to 21.4%.

recommendations: Lock in forward contracts for raw material procurement at fixed Q4 tariffs
Implement automated dynamic freight routing across Western corridor hub
Adjust Product A SKU pricing by +4.8% targeting premium urban demographics
Deploy automated optical inspection in line 3 to reduce warranty defect returns

messages.content: How will a 5% price increase on Product A affect our market share in South India?

Our elasticity model indicates South India has low price sensitivity (-0.42) for Product A due to strong brand equity. A 5% price increase generates ₹6.4 Cr incremental gross profit while reducing sales volume by only 1.8%, preserving a dominant 34.2% regional market share.
Identify vulnerabilities in our electronics component supply chain.
GraphRAG identified that 72% of microcontrollers route through a single tier-1 supplier in Taiwan. Lead times have lengthened from 45 to 68 days.
What are the top 3 Tier-2 cities for home appliances expansion?
Based on purchasing power parity and retail distributor capacity: 1. Coimbatore (+34% YoY demand), 2. Indore (+28%), 3. Surat (+25%).
Analyze why enterprise B2B customer churn rose in Q3.
Customer service tickets indicate 68% of churned accounts experienced delayed warranty servicing during August freight strikes.

slides.speakerScript: Respected Chairperson, internal examiners, and faculty members. Today our team presents our Major Project Phase-I Review on CORTEX: an Autonomous Multi-Agent Enterprise Decision Intelligence Platform with GraphRAG Knowledge Graphs and Predictive Scenario Simulation. We will demonstrate how our system solves enterprise decision latency through multi-agent consensus and graph-augmented reasoning.

slides.title: Table of Contents
slides.subtitle: 4-Phase Structured Presentation Agenda
slides.layoutTip: 4-Quadrant cards showing sequential progression across Foundation, Literature, Architecture, and Roadmap.
content: 1. FOUNDATION & CONTEXT: Introduction, Project Background, Problem Formulation, S.M.A.R.T. Objectives
2. LITERATURE & GAP ANALYSIS: Literature Survey, Existing System Workflows, Limitations & Gaps
3. PROPOSED SYSTEM & ARCHITECTURE: CORTEX Platform Overview, 5-Tier Methodology Architecture, Technology Stack
4. EXECUTION & PROGRESS: Phase-I Completed Work & Partial Results, Expected Outcomes, Semester Gantt Chart, References & Conclusion
slides.speakerScript: Our presentation follows four clear stages: establishing the strategic context and problem, reviewing seminal literature and existing gaps, detailing our five-tier proposed methodology and tech stack, and demonstrating our Phase-I prototype benchmarks alongside our Phase-II roadmap.

slides.title: Introduction
slides.subtitle: The Paradigm Shift in Enterprise Analytics
slides.layoutTip: Three horizontal progression cards: Descriptive BI (Past) -> Predictive ML (Trends) -> Prescriptive Decision Intelligence (Autonomous Action).
content: 1st Gen - Descriptive BI: SQL aggregations and retrospective charts ("What happened last quarter?")
2nd Gen - Predictive ML: Isolated forecasting models without cross-functional context ("What might revenue look like?")
3rd Gen - Decision Intelligence (CORTEX): Autonomous multi-agent reasoning with GraphRAG and what-if simulation ("What verified actions should we take, and what are the multi-order risks?")
Market Context: Gartner designates Decision Intelligence as a primary strategic technology; over 75% of Global 2000 firms will adopt DI by 2026.
slides.speakerScript: For decades, enterprise leadership has relied on passive dashboards. However, charts cannot make decisions. When a geopolitical or supply chain crisis happens, human executives must synthesize the data manually. CORTEX provides Decision Intelligence: an active operating system that reasons across documents and data to deliver audited, actionable choices.

slides.title: Background of the Project
slides.subtitle: Enterprise Data Explosion & Decision Latency
slides.layoutTip: Two-column layout: Unstructured Data Realities on left, Strategic Friction & Impact metrics on right.
content: Unstructured Enterprise Vastness: Over 80% of critical corporate intelligence resides in unstructured documents—vendor contracts, regulatory filings, logistics manifests, and board briefs.
Siloed Application Stack: Modern enterprises run separate systems for ERP (SAP), CRM (Salesforce), and Procurement (Oracle) that never talk to each other.
Decision Latency Crisis: Average enterprise takes 14 to 21 business days to cross-examine risk implications during international logistics or tariff shocks.
Financial Repercussion: Delayed strategic responses cost modern industrial firms an average of 4-7% in annual EBITDA erosion.
slides.speakerScript: Modern enterprises do not suffer from lack of data; they suffer from cognitive overload and systemic fragmentation. Crucial risk indicators exist in unstructured supplier PDFs, while financial metrics live in isolated ERP databases. When disruptions occur, it takes weeks to convene meetings and reach consensus, causing significant financial losses.

slides.title: Problem Statement
slides.subtitle: The Triple Bottleneck in Enterprise Decision-Making
slides.layoutTip: Three highlighted problem containers with alert accents detailing Semantic Myopia, Monolithic LLM Bias, and Static Spreadsheets.
content: 1. Semantic Myopia of Vector RAG: Standard vector search chunking fails at multi-hop reasoning across independent documents, resulting in hallucinated conclusions.
2. Lack of Dialectic Debate: Monolithic single-prompt LLMs lack fiduciary checks and balances, producing sycophantic advice without risk scrutiny.
3. Static Spreadsheets & BI: Legacy dashboards cannot dynamically recalculate margins, EBITDA, and OPEX in real-time under multi-variable parametric shifts.

Formal Statement: To engineer an autonomous decision intelligence platform providing sub-second multi-hop graph retrieval, multi-agent dialectic debate, and interactive parametric sensitivity simulation.
slides.speakerScript: We formulate our problem statement around three foundational flaws: first, naive vector RAG cannot trace multi-hop connections across documents; second, single LLM prompts fail because corporate strategy requires adversarial debate between growth, risk, and operations; and third, static BI dashboards cannot run live what-if parametric simulations.

slides.title: Aim and Objectives
slides.subtitle: S.M.A.R.T. Engineering Goals and Quantitative Targets
slides.layoutTip: Highlighted aim banner with 5 distinct objective cards displaying status badges.
content: PRIMARY AIM: To design, build, and benchmark an enterprise Decision Intelligence Platform uniting GraphRAG knowledge graphs, multi-agent dialectic debate, and dynamic sensitivity simulation.
Objective 1: Construct a multi-relational Knowledge Graph ontology linking suppliers, geographic nodes, and regulatory tariffs (Phase-I Target: Achieved).
Objective 2: Implement a 4-tier collaborative agent swarm (Strategy, Risk, Market, Operations) with consensus scoring (Phase-I Target: Achieved).
Objective 3: Engineer an interactive What-If parametric engine calculating real-time EBITDA and margin adjustments (Phase-I Target: Achieved).
Objective 4: Build a high-performance web workspace supporting dual-currency (INR Cr & USD M) and dynamic zoom ergonomics (Phase-I Target: Achieved).
Objective 5: Empirically benchmark multi-hop retrieval recall and hallucination reduction on enterprise datasets (Phase-II Target: Upcoming).
slides.speakerScript: Our primary aim is translated into five specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound objectives. During Phase-I, we successfully engineered the knowledge graph inspector, the responsive web workspace, the multi-agent UI, and the what-if mathematical simulator. Phase-II focuses on empirical benchmarking and real-time backend integration.

slides.title: Literature Review
slides.subtitle: Comparative Analysis of Seminal Research Papers
slides.layoutTip: Tabular literature matrix detailing Authors, Venue, Methodology, and Gaps addressed by CORTEX.
content: 1. Yao et al. (ICLR 2023) - "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models": Established agent reasoning traces, but focused on single-agent synthetic tasks without fiduciary debate.

2. Edge et al. / Microsoft (2024) - "From Local to Global: A GraphRAG Approach": Validated graph clustering over text chunks, but was batch-oriented and had high latency for interactive executive UIs.
3. Wu et al. / Microsoft (2023) - "AutoGen: Multi-Agent Conversation Framework": Proved multi-agent conversation potential, but lacked integrated deterministic financial simulation.
4. Gartner (2024) - "Strategic Technology Trends: Decision Intelligence": Formulated enterprise DI requirements theoretically without providing accessible open reference implementations.
Key Inference: Academic literature separates Knowledge Graphs, Multi-Agent Swarms, and Financial Simulators. CORTEX synthesizes all three into a single cohesive architecture.
slides.speakerScript: Our literature review examines four seminal publications. While Yao et al. pioneered ReAct and Edge et al. proved GraphRAG superiority, existing research keeps graph retrieval, agent debate, and financial mathematics in separate silos. CORTEX addresses this gap by creating an integrated neuro-symbolic platform.

slides.title: Existing System
slides.subtitle: Architecture & Workflow of Current Enterprise Solutions
slides.layoutTip: Process flow diagram contrasting Legacy BI tools and Ad-hoc Chatbots with high human intervention.
content: Component 1 - Legacy BI Platforms: Tableau, PowerBI, QlikView, Looker relying on pre-aggregated SQL cubes and static dashboards.
Component 2 - Naive Vector RAG Chatbots: Isolated bots using LangChain or LlamaIndex with basic text chunking and cosine similarity.
Component 3 - Manual Financial Spreadsheets: Massive Excel workbooks maintained by analyst teams with zero real-time linkage.
Workflow Flowchart: [Data Sources] -> [Batch ETL (24-48 hrs)] -> [SQL Dashboards] -> [Human Cognitive Load & Meetings] -> [Delayed Decisions].
slides.speakerScript: In existing enterprise workflows, operational data passes through slow batch ETL pipelines into static SQL dashboards. When an unexpected crisis strikes, executives are left to manually interpret charts, resulting in multi-week email chains and delayed strategic execution.

slides.title: Limitations of the Existing System
slides.subtitle: Systemic Vulnerabilities & Failure Points
slides.layoutTip: 4 Critical Failure Points with red alert tags: Multi-hop failure, Hallucination, Inflexibility, and Cognitive Overload.
content: 1. Multi-Hop Transitive Failure: Cannot trace indirect dependencies: (Supplier A) -> (Port B Strike) -> (Raw Material C) -> (Product Line D).
2. High Hallucination Risk: Unconstrained LLMs generate plausible but factually fictitious numbers when asked for financial estimates.
3. Complete Lack of Parametric What-If Simulation: Dashboards are read-only; executives cannot drag sliders to test energy or tariff fluctuations.
4. Single-Perspective Bias: A single prompt lacks the adversarial checks and balances of corporate governance where Risk must challenge Growth.
slides.speakerScript: We highlight four fatal flaws in existing systems: vector search fails at multi-hop walks across contracts; generic LLMs hallucinate numbers in financial contexts; dashboards lack interactive what-if simulation; and single prompts produce un-audited, risk-blind proposals.

slides.title: Proposed System
slides.subtitle: The CORTEX Decision Intelligence Platform
slides.layoutTip: Hero 4-Pillar Grid: Knowledge Core, Collaborative Agents, Sensitivity Simulator, and Action Workspace.
content: Pillar 1 - GraphRAG Knowledge Core: In-memory directed graph linking suppliers, logistical routes, contracts, and regulatory constraints with sub-50ms query traversals.
Pillar 2 - 4-Tier Collaborative Agent Swarm: Chief Strategy, Risk & Compliance, Market Trends, and Operations & Logistics agents running dialectic consensus.
Pillar 3 - Dynamic What-If Parametric Engine: Real-time mathematical sensitivity model adjusting revenue, OPEX, and EBITDA margins on the fly.
Pillar 4 - Verifiable Executive Workspace: Interactive UI with dual-currency INR/USD scaling, ergonomic display zoom, and one-click board dossier generation.
slides.speakerScript: To solve these issues, we propose CORTEX. CORTEX is not a simple chatbot; it is an autonomous digital strategy board. It maps enterprise dependencies onto an in-memory knowledge graph, deploys four specialized agents to deliberate over choices, and pairs this with a real-time what-if financial engine.

slides.title: Proposed Methodology / System Architecture
slides.subtitle: 5-Tier End-to-End Technical Pipeline
slides.layoutTip: Full architectural block diagram with data flows from Tier 1 Ingestion down to Tier 5 Workspace.
content: Tier 1 [Ingestion]: Unified intake of unstructured filings (PDF/Text) and structured records (ERP/CRM).
Tier 2 [GraphRAG Mesh]: Triplet extraction (Subject-Predicate-Object), in-memory adjacency lists, and community clustering.
Tier 3 [Multi-Agent Swarm]: ReAct debate protocol where Strategy, Risk, Market, and Operations agents propose, critique, and synthesize decisions.
Tier 4 [Predictive & Simulation Core]: Deterministic sensitivity modeling calculating parametric impact across pricing, energy, and labor.
Tier 5 [Executive Workspace]: React 19 UI with SVG graph physics, responsive viewport controls, dual-currency formatting, and printable dossiers.
slides.speakerScript: This slide presents our five-tier system architecture. Heterogeneous enterprise data is ingested in Tier 1, converted into an interconnected graph in Tier 2, deliberated by our 4-agent swarm in Tier 3, verified by the what-if simulation core in Tier 4, and presented in our responsive React 19 workspace in Tier 5.

slides.title: Tools and Technologies Used
slides.subtitle: Modern Production-Grade Engineering Stack
slides.layoutTip: 4-Column Tech Stack Grid: Frontend, AI Reasoning, Analytical Engine, and Development Infrastructure.
content: Frontend & UI: React 19, TypeScript 5.8, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide React, HTML5 Canvas & SVG Graph Renderer.
AI & Agent Orchestration: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro via Modern TypeScript SDK, ReAct Prompt Pipelines, Schema Validation.
Graph & Data Modeling: In-memory directed adjacency graph structures, JSON-LD schemas, Fast community walk algorithms.
Simulation & Math: Multivariate time-series regression algorithms, Parametric sensitivity matrix, Dual-currency INR/USD scaling.
DevOps & Build: Vite 6, Bun runtime, Node.js, ESLint, TypeScript Strict Compiler (Zero runtime type errors).
slides.speakerScript: We selected a modern, robust technology stack. The frontend utilizes React 19 with strict TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4, achieving 60 FPS rendering. Multi-agent reasoning uses Gemini models via the modern TypeScript SDK, backed by custom in-memory graph algorithms and Vite 6 build pipelines.

slides.title: Expected Outcomes
slides.subtitle: Phase-II Final Deliverables and Research Contributions
slides.layoutTip: 4 Deliverable Cards: Software Platform, Empirical Benchmark, Board Dossiers, and Research Paper.
content: 1. Complete Autonomous Decision Platform: Fully integrated, full-stack enterprise web application with role-based access control (RBAC).
2. Empirical Benchmark Study: Quantitative evaluation proving >35% higher multi-hop recall and >50% hallucination reduction over standard vector RAG.
3. Board-Ready PDF Decision Dossiers: One-click exportable C-suite executive briefing dossiers containing verified risk scores and audit trails.
4. Academic Research Publication: Final capstone thesis and submission to an IEEE/Scopus-indexed international conference on Artificial Intelligence.
slides.speakerScript: By the end of Phase-II, CORTEX will deliver four major outcomes: a complete full-stack decision intelligence application, a rigorous empirical benchmark demonstrating a 35% improvement in multi-hop accuracy, automated board-level PDF dossiers, and a peer-reviewed academic publication.
